newsitem.title: USA: Western Resources drops challenge to Tyco-ADT deal.
newsitem.headline: Western Resources drops challenge to Tyco-ADT deal.

text.p: Western Resources Inc. has dropped its court challenge to the proposed merger of Tyco International Ltd. and ADT Ltd., clearing the way for the $5.4 billion deal to go ahead, ADT said Thursday.
Western Resources had also bid for ADT, an electronic security services provider, and accumulated a 27 percent stake in the company as part of a hostile $3.5 billion takeover offer.

ADT said it had been informed by Western Resources that the spurned suitor no longer wished to block ADT's pact with Tyco, a maker of fire protection systems. Previously, Western filed suit in Florida and Bermuda seeking to stop the merger.
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission cleared the deal earlier this month.

Western's decision preserves accounting benefits associated with the Kansas-based utility's planned $2 billion acquisition of Kansas City Power and Light Co. Western struck a merger agreement with KCP&L in February, according to industry experts.
In a press release, ADT said Western, rather than fighting the Tyco-ADT deal in court, was "seeking its remedy in cash."
ADT officials were not available to elaborate.
